## Direct human PR lifecycle amendment

At2026-10-06T03:37UTC Matthew instructed: ΓÇ£In general we should close superceded PRs. We should also mark drafts as ready when they are labeled as ready for human review.ΓÇ¥

Effective for this authorized workflow: once a replacement PR is verified to carry the intended work and preserve required history/evidence, link original and replacement and close the superseded PR without merging or deleting its branch/evidence. Verify dependency targets and current owners before closure; do not close merely related or still-active work. Summary-only revisions update the existing current PR in place and do not justify a replacement.

Continue publishing new work as draft. When the coordinator verifies independent QA and all current readiness bindings and applies human-ready, also mark that open PR ready for review (draft=false), then reread revision/body/evidence/findings, label and draft state. Existing qualifying human-ready PRs should be reconciled to ready-for-review now. This is not an approving review, merge authorization or deployment. On later drift, remove readiness and update Project state under existing rules; this amendment does not authorize merging.

This direct instruction supersedes earlier blanket preservation of draft state on positive readiness transitions and instructions to keep known superseded drafts open. Preserve prior records and runtime pins; canonical guidance is being updated in its existing owned PR.
